title: Engine Feature Policy v1
description: Engine features this project bans outright, enforced repo-wide by the World Static Analysis Gate as a merge-blocking CI check. This policy exists because ordinary Godot idiom and the technology guidance carried in this project's own node context are multiplayer-oriented; a contributor following normal engine practice would add networking without intending to. The ban is mechanical, not advisory.
rationale: Single-player is a firm non-goal boundary in every phase. There is no network layer: no peers, no synchronizers, no authority checks, and no server-side validation scaffolding.
sourceOfTruth: The Engine Feature Policy contract on the World Static Analysis Gate node. This file is the machine-readable copy the gate loads; the multiplayer entry in contracts/sanctioned_api.v1.json mirrors it for world modules so core and worlds are covered by one ban.

scanScope.rationale: REQ-030 AC-2: the check scans core systems, official worlds, the reference template and community submissions — not world modules alone. A ban that covered only contributed code would leave the engine's own multiplayer idiom free to enter through core.

projectSettings: any multiplayer autoload or peer configuration in project.godot

projectSettingsPolicy.rationale: REQ-030 AC-5: project.godot must declare no networking or multiplayer autoloads, peer configuration, or network-related project settings. Parsed as INI rather than pattern-matched, so a setting cannot hide behind formatting.

enforcement.humanReview: This gate is a PRE-SCREEN, never a merge path. Branch protection requiring maintainer approval is configured by the CI Pipeline node; a green gate never merges on its own.

ruleIdNamespace.rationale: violations[].rule is a stable dotted id, never a message string, because that id is what an AI coding agent maps back to the contract element it broke.

violationOutput.requirement: REQ-030 AC-3: output names the specific API and the file. Every violation carries file, line, the exact symbol, and the dotted rule id.

guidanceOverride: Where general Godot documentation, engine samples, or catalog technology guidance demonstrate RPC-based movement or server-authority patterns, that guidance DOES NOT APPLY to this project. Implement movement, input, and state as local single-player logic. This project's own node packets carry such a sample in their Technology Guidance section; it is catalog boilerplate and is superseded by this policy.
